title: Comparison of Prognostic Utility and Additive Value of Quantitative Coronary Plaque Volumes Assessed with Coronary Computed Tomography Angiography and Quantitative Myocardial Ischemia Assessed by Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Imaging
summary:
In patients with suspected coronary artery disease (CAD), a computed tomography (CT) scan of the coronary arteries is frequently performed. This study evaluates coronary CT images to investigate whether precise quantification and analysis of plaque composition in the coronary arteries can improve the assessment of future cardiac risks (such as heart attacks or the need for revascularization). The study utilizes the world’s latest generation of CT scanners (photon-counting CT), enabling detailed analysis of even the smallest plaque components comparable to intracoronary imaging. All coronary CT scans are performed based on clinical indications in accordance with the guideline recommendations of the European Society of Cardiology.
The aim is to determine whether a detailed plaque analysis allows for more targeted treatment and prevention of cardiovascular diseases. The study is purely observational, meaning that no additional examinations or interventions are carried out.

interventions.name: Patients who underwent coronary computed tomography angiography for a clinical indications.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Coronary CT (with photon-counting CT) based on clinical indication
2. Written consent for the pseudonymized use of clinical, procedural, and follow-up data
Exclusion criteria:
1) acute myocardial infarction
2) incomplete CCTA examination of the coronary arteries (e.g. no contrast medium given due to high Agatston-Score, renal insufficiency, or allergy) or insufficient CCTA image quality
3) co-morbidities with life-expectancy < 2 years
